A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with SYGAR renamed Compositional-ARC. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLC and LLM evaluations, experiments across four data splits, component ablations, and a static-grammar training experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of ARC-specialized LLMs, including comparisons with and without test-time training.

M1.justification: The proposed MLC procedure retains the same patch encoding, positional embeddings, encoder-decoder architecture, auxiliary copy task, weighted loss, and target perturbations. Expanded episode explanations clarify the existing method; test-time training is introduced for comparison models.

E1.justification: SYGAR becomes Compositional-ARC, retaining the same generated grid domain, five transformations, three-shot and systematicity tasks, and static-grammar experiment. ARC-related datasets newly discussed in v2 describe comparator pretraining, rather than additional benchmark evaluations conducted by this work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Llama-3.2-3B-ReARC and Mistral-NeMO-Minitron-8B-Full to both tasks, plus test-time-trained variants in the systematicity comparison. The original general-purpose LLM comparators and Appendix D's basic seq2seq comparison remain.

E3.justification: The new specialist evaluations introduce augmented inference, candidate pruning, and one-epoch LoRA adaptation using test study examples repeated 48 times. TTT is explicitly excluded from three-shot evaluation to preserve held-out compositions. Existing splits, metrics, and API settings remain; Appendix D changes the static model's stated training unit from 200 episodes to 200 epochs, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds with/without-TTT analyses for both ARC specialists, testing whether adaptation on lower-level transformations enables systematic generalization. Figures 3–8 extend the qualitative comparisons, and Figure 4 replaces its example episode. Existing MLC ablations, split-consistency checks, and the static-grammar analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same means and standard deviations across four data splits, with the same seeds documented in Table 5. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is reported for the added baselines.

E6.justification: New Table 1 exact-match scores for Llama/Mistral are 85.85%/95.71% in three-shot evaluation, 0.87%/0.70% in systematicity without TTT, and 73.70%/78.20% with TTT. Existing aggregate scores remain unchanged. Table 4 and the qualitative figures add specialist results. v2's Section 5 gives Llama's non-TTT score as 0.70%, inconsistent with Table 1's 0.87%.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2's rotation definition replaces the joint minimum with separate coordinate minima and swaps the signed rotation formulas. However, its final transformed-object expression now omits applying the rotation to the offsets and returns unrotated coordinates as printed. This is a substantive but localized mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion add the claim that the 5.7M-parameter MLC model matches the ARC Prize 2024 winning 8B model with TTT. v2 explicitly distinguishes outperforming general-purpose LLMs from matching adapted specialists, substantially extending the comparative contribution.

C2.justification: v2 hypothesizes that TTT teaches specialists to abstract and compose transformations from lower-level examples, and explains why three-shot TTT would compromise the intended generalization test. Appendix D also adds a categorical claim that systematicity requires dynamically varying grammars, based on the unchanged static-training result.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds specialist checkpoint identifiers, code-access references, and detailed augmentation, pruning, and LoRA settings. Existing MLC hyperparameters and compute descriptions remain. The reproducibility statement drops v1's statement that example API queries and responses are included in supplementary material.

R1.justification: v2 adds Franzen et al. (2024), Hodel (2024), and Li et al. (2025) around the specialist comparisons and positions MLC alongside ARC Prize solvers. Irie and Lake (2024) is removed. The broader related-work discussion remains largely intact; several other references receive publication metadata updates.

P1.justification: The title and dataset name change, and focused rewrites clarify episodes and distinguish general-purpose from domain-specific LLMs. Appendix E adds an AI-assistance disclosure. Main section ordering and most background, method, and appendix prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 expand and regroup comparisons, while Figures 3–8 substantially rearrange query and prediction panels to accommodate specialists. Table 3 becomes two parallel parameter blocks, table captions move above their tables, and Figures 9–10 share a page. Typography and headers also change throughout.

improvement.justification: Adding relevant ARC-specialized solvers and documented TTT controls addresses v1's limited main comparator coverage and better qualifies MLC's relative capabilities. These gains outweigh localized regressions, but the net improvement is limited by the broken rotation expression in Definition 3, the Llama text/table score mismatch, and the stronger necessity claim drawn from the unchanged static-grammar experiment.
